caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular wooden box featuring intricate geometric patterns and inlaid designs on its surfaces. The box predominantly showcases shades of brown, tan, beige, and black, with the wood grain visibly rendered throughout. The lid of the box is decorated with a series of nested rectangular and diamond shapes, each bordered by fine, alternating color bands and detailed motifs. The front panel includes a central keyhole with a white plate, positioned above two circular star-like inlays, which are encased in diamond shapes. The borders of the box, including the edges and corners, are accentuated with alternating checkered and zigzag patterns in black, tan, and lighter hues. The side panels of the box continue the theme of geometric and checkered decorations. The overall composition is symmetrical and the drawing is oriented to show the front and top of the box, as well as part of one side. At the bottom right corner of the image, the words "FRANCIS LAVIS DURANO" are inscribed in small, capital letters.
title: Inlaid Sewing Box
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
